'''''Wahlenbergia hederacea''''', also known as the '''ivy-leaved bellflower''', is a species of flowering plant that is found throughout Europe. The delicate, patch-forming, hairless perennial herb has thin, creeping stems about 20 cm in length. Its pale green leaves are long-stalked and have an ivy-shaped, rounded structure. These leaves can be described as having a [[Cordate (leaf shape)|cordate]] shape and are approximately 5–12 mm long and wide. The plant has erect, solitary, pale blue flowers in summer and autumn,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hardy Flowers|last=Robinson|first=William|publisher=Applewood Books|year=2009|isbn=9781429014434|pages=261}}</ref> with bell-shaped [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]] with 5 short lobes.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaofho10ever|title=The New York Botanical Garden illustrated encyclopedia of horticulture|last=Everett|first=Thomas H.|publisher=Taylor & Francis|others=New York Botanical Garden.|year=1982|isbn=9780824072407|volume=10|location=New York|pages=[https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaofho10ever/page/3521 3521]|url-access=registration}}</ref> The flowers are 6–10 mm long x 5–8 mm wide<ref>The Wild Flower Key, British Isles N.W. Europe, Francis Rose, WARNE, Published by the Penguin Group, 1991 reissue, {{ISBN|0-7232-2419-6}}</ref> and sit on fine stalks 1–4 cm long. It is suggested that the long [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] are an adaptation to assist in seed dispersal.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Eddie|first1=William|last2=Cupido|first2=Christopher|date=March 2014|title=Hesperocodon, a new generic name for Wahlenbergia hederacea (Campanulaceae): phylogeny and capsule dehiscence|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260330806|journal=Edinburgh Journal of Botany|volume=71|issue=1|pages=63–74|doi=10.1017/s0960428613000310|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
This species was first formally described in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]] who gave it the name ''[[Campanula hederacea]]'' in his ''[[Species Plantarum]]''.<ref name="POWO1">{{cite web |title=''Campanula hederaceae'' |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:140407-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref><ref name="L.">{{cite book |last1=Linnaeus |first1=Carl |title=Species Plantarum |date=1753 |publisher=Junk |location=Berlin |page=169 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/84235#page/183/mode/1up |access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref> In 1827, [[Ludwig Reichenbach]] transferred the species to ''Wahlenbergia'' as ''W. hederacea'' in his ''Iconographia Botanica''.<ref name="POWO" /><ref name="Rchb.">{{cite book |last1=Reichenbach |first1=Ludwig |title=Iconographia Botanica sea Plantae Criticae |date=1827 |publisher=Apud Fridericum Hofmeister |location=Leipzig |page=47 |url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/10429/?offset=#page=55&viewer=picture&o=bookmark&n=0&q= |access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref>

==Habitat==
''Wahlenbergia hederacea'' is found in cool, moist and boggy, partially-shaded areas,<ref name=":0" /> typically with acidic soils, such as woodlands, streams, pastures, heaths and beside [[rivulet]]s. The plant thrives in short-grassed areas beside streams, with moist, acidic soils, and is almost never found in basic soils and stagnant water.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Rix|first=Martyn|date=26 February 2004|title=Plate 488. Wahlenbergia hederacea|journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine|volume=21|issue=1|pages=61–64|doi=10.1111/j.1467-8748.2004.00413.x}}</ref> They usually occur in small, scattered groups. The abundance of the ivy-leaved bellflower has been declining throughout the 1900s due to the loss of their habitat.<ref name=":1" />

==Distribution==
''Wahlenbergia hederacea'' is native to Europe and commonly found in southern England, and [[Wales]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/wahlenbergia-hederacea|title=Wahlenbergia hederacea {{!}} Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora|website=www.brc.ac.uk|language=en}}</ref> but also in [[North West England]], Western Scotland, Ireland, France, Belgium, Netherlands, [[Luxembourg]], Western Germany, Spain, and Portugal.<ref name=":2" />
